alignments.note: Third-person imperative rendered periphrastically: the auxiliary *let* and the supplied subject *him* are rule 7/9 helpers on the inflected verb, and rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical verb *know* rather than on the auxiliary or the supplied subject. Rule 73's `κόπους … μηδεὶς παρεχέτω` → *let no man trouble me* keeps such an imperative *let* inside the verb's own unit.
Rule 43's test is the English: the ASV renders the clause as reported speech and writes *that*, so the conjunction is aligned to that word in the ordinary way rather than left `unrepresented`.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun and nothing else. The ASV writes two English words, *he who*, so rule 90's single-relativizer case does not apply and the ordinary split holds, as rule 90 itself says of *He* / *that would*.
The participle is what the relative clause is predicated of, so the supplied relativizer *who* is its rule 7 helper under rule 32, and rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical verb *converteth*.

Anarthrous substantival adjective: no article competes, so the supplied indefinite is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines under rule 51's anarthrous clause. The English is a single noun glossing the lexeme rather than a generic completion, so rule 17 heads it on *sinner*.
Expressed preposition realized by the English preposition governing the phrase, under rule 36.
No Greek article stands here, so under rule 51's anarthrous clause the supplied *the* is a rule 7 helper on the noun it determines rather than an article's own determiner, and the head is the noun.

Genitive noun rendered *of … way*. No article stands to anchor a determiner, so rule 21's determinerless clause keeps the case preposition with the noun; the unit is discontinuous around the possessive under rule 15, and rule 17 heads a source noun rendered *of + noun* on the noun.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *his*. Rule 20's displacement is not in question, no article standing before `ὁδοῦ` for the possessive to empty.
Future indicative: *shall* is the rule 9 auxiliary helper and rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical verb *save*.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines.

The ASV writes *a soul*, not *his soul*, so this second genitive pronoun has no English realization and is its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23. The projection carries the pronoun and SBLGNT.JAS.5.20.v020 is not marked FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE, so rule 97 is not in play and rule 12 forbids treating the ASV's silence as a textual decision. A reference comparison will report this token as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
Expressed preposition realized by *from* under rule 36.
Bare noun to bare noun; the ASV supplies no determiner, so nothing else rides in this unit.
Expressed conjunction coordinating the two future indicatives, aligned to *and* in the ordinary way. Rules 88 and 98 do not arise, the juncture being written in the Greek.
Future indicative: *shall* is the rule 9 auxiliary helper and the head is the lexical verb *cover*.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 7/51 helper.
Genitive noun rendered *of sins*; rule 17 heads a source noun rendered *of + noun* on the noun, the case preposition riding with it under rule 21's determinerless clause.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged: every unit of the accepted alignment survives review. Notes were expanded where the governing rule was implicit, but no unit's source array, target array, head or status changed.
Partition verified by enumeration: s001-s018 each appear exactly once, and t001-t028 each appear exactly once across the eighteen units. No id is invented.

s003/s004 stays split under rule 32 rather than joined under rule 90. Rule 90 is scoped in terms to where the ASV writes only *one* English word for the article-plus-participle pair; here it writes two (*he who*), and rule 90's own closing clause sends the two-word case back to the ordinary split.

s008 is the one discontinuous unit: *of … way* wraps around *his*. Rule 15 permits it, and the alternative of putting *of* on the possessive or on `ἐκ` is refused by rule 21's determinerless clause, which keeps a case preposition with the noun where no article stands to anchor a determiner.

s012 is the verse's only `unrepresented` unit. Both variant units selected r00-base and neither carries a FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE mark, so rule 97 is not in play and rule 12 bars reading the ASV's *a soul* as a textual decision against the projection's `αὐτοῦ`. A reference comparison will report s012 as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.

Head choices were reviewed independently of edges under rule 28: the three finite verbs and the imperative head on their lexical verbs rather than on *shall* or *let*, and the four supplied-determiner units head on their nouns rather than on *a* or *the*, since rule 51's anarthrous clause makes those determiners helpers and not article realizations.
